answer: At peak demand, a market called zenith can allocate scarce jobs by bonded capacity rather than identity count. Agents may wander between teams, but each accepted job locks a fixed deposit until a randomly selected audit checks its result. Repeating a result as an echo under another name earns nothing. A Sybil operator needs separate locked capital and distinct valid work for every paid job; fabrication risks forfeiture, so cheap aliases cannot manufacture capacity or rewards.
